freshAdmission.observation: Originally PAY_PER_REQUEST MREC global table with one KEYS_ONLY GSI and no prior scaling history accepts UpdateTable to PROVISIONED with table and GSI R2W2. Both regions settle ACTIVE at actual table and GSI R2W2. This admission does not require caller-preconfigured write autoscaling.

generatedResources.initialPolicyOptionalFields: ScaleInCooldown, ScaleOutCooldown and DisableScaleIn absent in returned configuration

freshAdmission.bound: Source snapshot126 started 2026-09-18T21:01:38.568043+00:00, about246 seconds after admission53; peer snapshot131 started about250 seconds after admission. No claim of fixed timing or account-independent max quota.

onDemandVisibility.observation: On-demand mode reports table/GSI provisioned capacity zero but preserves visible AAS targets and policies, including distinctive source/peer bounds, utilization, cooldowns, DisableScaleIn, target suspension flags and target tags. All eight known target ARN tag lookups succeed. Billing-mode inactivity must not be modeled as disappearing targets/policies or inferred from AAS SuspendedState.
onDemandVisibility.bound: Both-region on-demand snapshot224-233 spans 2026-09-18T21:05:38.579278+00:00 onward, about100-109 seconds after switch195; subsequent owned operations provide additional bounded observations.

onDemandOwnedOperations.observation: DeleteScalingPolicy and DeregisterScalableTarget for the owned peer GSI-read dimension succeed while on-demand. The old peer read target is absent from describe and known ARN ListTagsForResource returns ResourceNotFoundException274. Other target tags remain accessible. Attempted source table-read bounds update and policy update are rejected as PAY_PER_REQUEST table mode is not scalable; no accepted suspended-state edits to these settings occurred.

returnToProvisioned.observation: Return with explicit table/GSI R2W2 resets target bounds to2/40000 and generated-name target-tracking policies to70 in both regions. Distinct source/peer bounds and policy utilization/cooldowns/DisableScaleIn do not survive this path. Seven undeleted target ARNs, tags and nondefault SuspendedState survive. Their policy ARNs also compare equal, but CloudTrail proves DeleteScalingPolicy then PutScalingPolicy, so equal ARN is not proof of uninterrupted policy preservation. Deleted peer GSI-read is recreated with new target/policy ARNs, empty tags and all-false SuspendedState; its old ARN remains NotFound. Actual table/GSI capacity is R2W2.
returnToProvisioned.bound: Restored bounded source snapshot304 starts about99 seconds after admission277; peer snapshot309 about103 seconds after. No indefinite-state or timing guarantee inferred.

customPolicyName.bound: Second switch to on-demand339 succeeds; no rate-restricted switch was retried and no second table was necessary. Custom restored bounded source policy snapshot395 started94.077 seconds after return368.

cloudTrailOwnership.observation: Generated RegisterScalableTarget and PutScalingPolicy calls use AWSServiceRoleForDynamoDBReplication/ProdReplDynamoSession and invokedBy replication.dynamodb.amazonaws.com. On return, observed DeleteScalingPolicy calls use customer IAM user Delegated with invokedBy dynamodb.amazonaws.com. singleOwnerImplications.classification: inference bounded by observed public calls
implications: Keep scalable-target identity, bounds, tags, flags, policies and alarm lifecycle authoritative in the existing AAS owner rather than a second DynamoDB historical settings store.
On-demand table capacity and scalable-target existence are different properties: targets/policies remain queryable and deletable, while create/update admission fails for the on-demand resource.

Observed provisioned entry is a coordinated standard-control sequence: remove existing policies, register/update targets with explicit new min and max but omitted tags/flags, and put generated default policies; deleted targets get new identities and existing targets preserve omitted fields.
Do not interpret stable policy ARN across the mode round-trip as proof of retained policy configuration; CloudTrail explicitly records deletion and replacement.
The native40000 max is an observed account/region default, not evidence to hardcode a universal quota or invent missing quota infrastructure.

limitations: One empty owned MREC version2019 global table, one GSI, two US regions. No data/load, metric-triggered scale-in/out, scheduled actions, legacy, MRSC, encryption or untiered replica-autoscaling API experiments.

All findings are bounded snapshots and owned CloudTrail records, not promises of AWS convergence time or exhaustive event history. CloudTrail queries retained only events containing the exact unique owned table name; unrelated records were discarded.
The source/peer overrides tested here are direct regional AAS target/policy configurations, not UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling replica override inputs.
Generated default-name configurations were tested for all four dimensions in both regions; custom-name replacement was tested for source table-read only.

One STS identity read had a client connect timeout at sequence366. A fresh subprocess retried identity verification before any custom restoration mutation; no mutation was retried after uncertain transport.
